text:
anya: noticing steady mem growth on long chat contexts in prod, trending up over a few hours. heap snapshots show kv_pages growing instead of stabilizing. :confused:
anya: short repro in staging attached below. seems tied to repeated prefix prompts and mixed small/big batches.
anya: repro steps:
```
1) start long-run worker with batch_size=8, continuous streams
2) send alternating short (10 tokens) and long (1200 tokens) requests that share prefixes
3) observe kv_page_count++ and rss growth ~ +200MB/hour
```
matt: hmm could be slab fragmentation or eviction not freeing orphaned slots. did you see any eviction logs?
anya: eviction logs show tombstones but we still see pages referenced in active_page_map with stale request_ids. example: `page=0x7fabc... refs=1 last_owner=req:0xdeadbeef` but that req id is from >10s ago.
sree: this sounds like the slot reuse race we thought we fixed in #197. could the batch splitter be returning partially filled frames and skipping proper tag rotation?
laura: I ran the perf flame on staging during repro. kernel selection toggles (int8->fp16) when sequence > 512. when that flip happens mid-stream for a request we saw misaligned writes to the kv buffer (offset computed with old layout). attached li lines: `kv_write: offset=24576 len=512 owner=req:0xaba` then later `kv_write: offset=24576 len=64 owner=req:0xbad` -> same offset different owner.
sam: so alignment+kernel flip -> same offset allocated twice without proper fence? :eyes:
anya: reproducer log (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-18T14:01:02Z] req=0x001 alloc_page page_id=42 offset=0x6000 len=512 owner=req=0x001
[2026-03-18T14:01:02Z] req=0x002 kernel_switch int8->fp16
[2026-03-18T14:01:02Z] req=0x002 kv_write page_id=42 offset=0x6000 len=64 owner=req=0x002
[2026-03-18T14:01:02Z] evict page_id=42 tombstone set
[2026-03-18T14:01:03Z] req=0x003 read page_id=42 offset=0x6000 -> returns stale tokens from req=0x002
```
laura: that last line shows cross-request contamination. also memory not reclaimed because refs still present.
matt: could be missing memory_barrier or missing atomic update of owner tag. I remember race where kernel branch writes smaller partial chunk but doesn't update the slot fingerprint.
sree: another angle: batching heuristics merge small requests into a continuous batch and the KV write for merged batch uses aggregated offset calc that doesn't respect per-request alignment. I can add assertions to verify owner tag != current_req when writing.
anya: tests: i added a debug assert in build that checks `if (slot.owner != current_req) crash` and repro hits it in ~30s.
sam: nice. can we make a minimal unit test that simulates kernel flip? maybe mock kernel_selector to force flip at token 512 and alternate lengths.
perf-bot: CI perf run failed: kv-tests::owner-assert (signal: SIGABRT) on linux-x86_64 || see https://ci.internal/runs/3291
laura: where to land fix? options:
- ensure owner tag is updated atomically with write and add a seqno to detect reuse
- make batch splitter enforce alignment boundaries when merging different kernel regimes
- add reclamation pass that reclaims pages whose owner doesn't match any active req after X seconds
matt: prefer owner-tag atomicity + seqno. that should be minimal and correct. splitting rules are more invasive. reclamation is bandaid.
sree: i'll prototype owner-tag+seqno. quick plan: extend slot header with 16-bit epoch, increment on alloc, atomically compare-exchange header on write. fallbacks use epoch mismatch to refuse reuse.
anya: fyi this will also add small header overhead (~8 bytes/slot) but we'll offset by freeing orphaned refs faster.
laura: also run long-run memtest for 6h after patch to ensure no slow leak. integrate perf bot smoke nightly.
sam: i'll open an RFC PR for batching changes once v1 fix merged.
anya: assigning to sree, matt to review. created issue https://redwood/issues/INF-4123 and pinned logs there. :white_check_mark:
matt: ack. thanks for the detailed repro — huge help.
sree: working on prototype, will push an experimental branch later today.
anya: great, please ping when ready and I'll run staging long-run.
laura: also set alert rule to trigger if kv_page_count increases > 5% over 30m for high-traffic workers.
perf-bot: alert created: KV_PAGE_COUNT_HIGH -> severity=warning
sam: cool. hope this kills the cross-request stale-block issue.
anya: thanks everyone. will update the issue with staging mem snapshots after sree's branch lands.
